MAKE DOC: Changing the oil in a lawn mower engine
## Before you start
Run the engine for two minutes so the oil flows, then switch it off and pull the spark plug lead.
## You need
- A drain pan and a funnel
- 0.6 litres of SAE 30 oil
## Steps
1. Tip the mower with the air filter facing up, or open the drain plug.
2. Let the old oil drain into the pan.
3. Refit the plug and pour in the new oil a little at a time.
4. Check the dipstick and top up to the full mark.
## Afterwards
Take the old oil to a recycling point; never pour it on the ground.
END

MAKE DOC: Fixing a flat bicycle tyre
## You need
- Two tyre levers
- A patch kit and a pump
## Steps
1. Take the wheel off the bike and let out any air left in the tube.
2. Lever one side of the tyre off the rim and pull the inner tube out.
3. Pump the tube up and find the hole by its hiss, or in a bowl of water.
4. Roughen the area, spread the glue, wait a minute, then press the patch on firmly.
5. Put the tube back, refit the tyre with your thumbs and pump it to the pressure on the tyre wall.
## Afterwards
Check inside the tyre for the thorn or glass that made the hole before you ride.
END

# Ladder safety
A five-minute toolbox talk.
# Before you climb
- Check the feet, rungs and locks
- Set it on firm, level ground
# Set it up right

- Tie it off or have it footed
# On the ladder
- Keep three points of contact
- Never stand on the top two rungs
# Remember
- Check it, set it, climb it safely
END

MAKE WHEEL: Ohm's law power wheel
P watts: P = V x I | P = V^2 / R | P = I^2 x R
V volts: V = I x R | V = P / I | V = sqrt(P x R)
I amps: I = V / R | I = P / V | I = sqrt(P / R)
R ohms: R = V / I | R = V^2 / P | R = P / I^2
END
